Review this exact FG-177 helper-shadowing repair. Requirements: Sandbox.admitCall remains the authoritative FreeCall precedence (script-defined helper/Builtin before registered hosted Step); a hosted branch halt must terminate Groovy evaluation without invoking any later helper/builtin/step, discarding arguments into a zero-arity helper call, forcing missing or effectful arguments, or replacing the original host diagnostic. A halt caused by a nested argument or by Perform must unwind immediately. Batch mode behavior remains unchanged. Method and safe-method calls cannot route as hosted steps but must also stop after a hosted branch halt. Tests must prove helpers named like vocabulary steps both shadow while live and stay wholly unobserved after halt; pinned Jenkins differential remains result/output/workspace equivalent. No later FG-177 return slice may be implemented. Identify concrete precedence, unwinding, catchability, scope, or regression gaps only. +The validation boundary is also downstream of the branch-halt guard. For a
+`FreeCall`, the interpreter first applies the authoritative sandbox resolution:
+a script-defined helper wins over a registered hosted step. Reachability is
+then branch-wide, not step-name-based. It is checked before every call argument

+evaluation without creating an interpreter fault. Consequently a later helper
+named `sh`, `echo`, or another hosted step is neither invoked with discarded
+arguments nor allowed to evaluate missing-property or effectful arguments.
